rehomed.assertion: The shelf's list is asked again every SHELF_REFRESH_MS while the tab is visible: the host's react-query timer behind useDeliverables' refetchInterval (the kit asserts the option and what a new page shows).

Load more sends the next page's offset (24) and limit with the chip's artifact_type and source_type_exclude=heartbeat on the wire: the host's buildListQuery (the kit asserts the filters and that the shelf asks for the next page).

A list page that answers success: false is the query's error, thrown by the host's hook and never a page, and a failed refetch or Load more keeps the loaded pages (the kit asserts what the shelf shows and logs for that answer).
/deliverables?deliverable=<id> opens that Deliverable: the host's deep link (the kit asserts the link each card carries).
Start a chat opens a fresh draft beside the stored tabs and goes to /chat: the host's useStartChat (the kit asserts the shelf calls it).

rewritten: The SDK is the stand-in (test/sdk-stub.ts): useDeliverables answers what the test sets, as react-query would, instead of core's mocked hook or its real hook over a mocked apiClient, so the real-hook cases keep their Play assertions and name core's tests for the host's part (rehomed); the seen record is written and read through the SDK storage area (writeSeen, readSeen), not the automatos-play:seen-deliverables key; the workspace, the backend's health, Start a chat and the pictures come from the stand-in's controls.

rehomed.assertion: DeliverableDeepLink stays closed under the theme at its width: /deliverables?deliverable=<id>, and the backend's ?tab=outputs&deliverable=<id>, open the theme's page for that Deliverable through the host's deliverables layout (the kit asserts PlayShelf shows the page the link names).
DeliverableDeepLink opens as before under a core style and below the theme's width, with the core page, and the theme's page never asks for the Deliverable: the host's deliverables layout.
Below the theme's width the Deliverables layout keeps the core page and its deep link for a ?deliverable= link, and the theme's page never mounts.

The detail is asked on the wire as /api/deliverables/<id>?include_content=true: the host's useDeliverable (the kit asserts PlayDeliverable asks useDeliverable(id, true) and shows the content the backend answers).

Download fetches a text file's raw route, never its content route's JSON, and a raw route as it is, with the caller's token, saved under the file's name: the host's deliverableDownloadUrl, fileDownloadUrl and useFileDownload (the kit asserts the route, the name and the words Play hands the download).

A failed download says Play's own words (DOWNLOAD_FAILED), never the host's default, and saves nothing: the host's useFileDownload (the kit asserts Play gives it those words, from the file card and the side panel).

The sheet's markdown becomes elements (headings, strong, a table) and its fenced code a <pre>: the host's MarkdownView (the kit asserts the text Play hands it, and Play's pre and img rules on their own).
MarkdownView drops raw HTML for skipHtml and applies the theme's element overrides: the host's renderer under the SDK card (the kit asserts Play hands it skipHtml and PLAY_MARKDOWN_COMPONENTS).

rewritten: The SDK is the harness's fake (packages/theme-harness): useDeliverable answers what the test sets (host.setDetail) or the scripted backend's rows (host.setDeliverables, its 404 for an unknown id), instead of core's mocked hook or its real hook over a mocked apiClient; the query string, the pictures (host.setBlobUrls) and the downloads (host.downloadsAsked, with the words for a failure) are the fake host's; the host's MarkdownView is a stand-in, so the sheet's cases assert the props Play hands it (host.markdownViews) and Play's element rules rendered alone; DeliverableDeepLink in the host's layout and the request on the wire are core's (rehomed).
